review.summary: Mercedes lead the constructors with 578 points across 17 rounds, eleven wins and 22 podiums. Andrea Kimi Antonelli tops the drivers' standings ahead of George Russell, so their advantage rests on steady scoring from both cars rather than a single driver.
review.lastRace: Andrea Kimi Antonelli took a podium in Singapore, finishing third from fourth on the grid for 15 points, while George Russell recovered to ninth after starting 19th for two points.

review.summary: Ferrari are second with 444 points from 17 rounds and two wins. Lewis Hamilton leads their drivers ahead of Charles Leclerc in the standings, a gap that keeps the pair close together.
review.lastRace: Charles Leclerc finished second off his starting spot for a full podium's worth of 18 points, while Lewis Hamilton dropped to sixth from third for eight.

review.summary: McLaren are third with 339 points and two wins across 17 rounds. Lando Norris leads the pair comfortably ahead of Oscar Piastri, both having scored regularly to stay in the mix.
review.lastRace: Both cars finished in the points, Norris fourth for 12 from fifth on the grid and Piastri fifth for 10 after starting sixth.

review.summary: Red Bull are fourth with 332 points and two wins over 17 rounds. Max Verstappen carries the team's charge well clear of Isack Hadjar, who trails further down the standings.
review.lastRace: Max Verstappen won from pole for a full 25 points, while Isack Hadjar picked up his lone point by finishing tenth after starting 22nd.

review.summary: RB F1 Team are fifth with 100 points from 17 rounds and no wins or podiums. Arvid Lindblad leads their drivers well clear of Yuki Tsunoda, who has barely added to the total.
review.lastRace: Liam Lawson took the team's only points with a seventh-place finish from eighth on the grid for six, while Arvid Lindblad was lapped in fifteenth after starting ninth without scoring.

review.summary: Alpine are sixth with 68 points and no wins or podiums across 17 rounds. Pierre Gasly leads the pair having outscored Franco Colapinto so far this season.

review.summary: Haas are seventh with 30 points and nothing on the board in wins or podiums. Oliver Bearman leads their drivers ahead of Esteban Ocon, who has struggled to keep pace.
review.lastRace: Both cars were lapped, Oliver Bearman twelfth from eleventh and Esteban Ocon thirteenth from twelfth, neither reaching the points.

review.summary: Audi are eighth with 23 points and no wins or podiums. Nico Hülkenberg leads the pair just ahead of Gabriel Bortoleto, both having picked up small totals this season.
review.lastRace: Nico Hülkenberg scored four points by finishing eighth after starting tenth, while Gabriel Bortoleto retired from fourteen on the grid without points.

review.summary: Williams are ninth with 12 points and nothing on the board. Carlos Sainz sits just ahead of Alexander Albon in their drivers' standings, both having scored sparingly this season.
review.lastRace: Carlos Sainz was lapped in fourteenth after starting thirteenth without scoring, while Alexander Albon retired from sixteenth on the grid for zero points.

review.summary: Aston Martin are tenth with just 7 points and no wins or podiums. Fernando Alonso is their sole scorer, well ahead of Lance Stroll who has failed to add to the total.
review.lastRace: Fernando Alonso was lapped in sixteenth after starting twentieth without scoring, while Lance Stroll retired from twenty-first on the grid for zero points.

review.summary: Cadillac are eleventh with no points across 17 rounds and no wins or podiums. Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Pérez sit at the back of the standings having failed to score, so there is little to separate them.
review.lastRace: Both cars were lapped, Sergio Pérez in seventeenth from seventeenth and Valtteri Bottas nineteenth from eighteenth, neither reaching the points.

review.lastRace: A breakthrough London E-Prix for DS Penske. Barnard drove from sixth to victory, taking 25 points, while Günther fell from fourteenth to eleventh without scoring.

Max Verstappen of Red Bull won from pole in Singapore, holding off Charles Leclerc of Ferrari by seven seconds for second with the fastest lap, while Mercedes' Andrea Kimi Antonelli took third. The front-row start paid off as Verstappen led home a McLaren one-two of Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri. Four drivers retired - Alexander Albon, Lance Stroll, Franco Colapinto and Gabriel Bortoleto - while several others were lapped.
highlights: Isack Hadjar made the biggest climb of the race, starting 22nd and finishing tenth for Red Bull to gain twelve places.
Charles Leclerc set the fastest lap of the Singapore Grand Prix while finishing second for Ferrari behind winner Max Verstappen.
Four drivers retired without completing the race: Alexander Albon, Lance Stroll, Franco Colapinto and Gabriel Bortoleto.

review.summary: Marco Bezzecchi won the Grand Prix of Indonesia for Aprilia Racing, with Raul Fernandez second for SuperFile Trackhouse MotoGP Team and Jorge Martin third for Aprilia Racing. Ai Ogura completed the front four for SuperFile Trackhouse, Pedro Acosta fifth for KTM and Marc Marquez sixth for Ducati Lenovo Team. Francesco Bagnaia, Fermin Aldeguer, Toprak Razgatlioglu and Jack Miller all failed to finish.
highlights: Marco Bezzecchi won the Grand Prix of Indonesia for Aprilia Racing on 25 points.
Raul Fernandez finished second for SuperFile Trackhouse MotoGP Team, with Jorge Martin third for Aprilia Racing.
Pedro Acosta was fifth for Red Bull KTM Factory Racing and Marc Marquez sixth for Ducati Lenovo Team.
Francesco Bagnaia, Fermin Aldeguer, Toprak Razgatlioglu and Jack Miller all failed to finish.

review.summary: Barnard took a late victory at London, climbing from sixth on the grid past the field for DS Penske. De Vries completed the drive from pole to second for Mahindra and Mortara was third from second, giving Mahindra a one-two. The classification also exposed front-row fades as Wehrlein fell from third to fourteenth and Müller slipped from fourth to twelfth.
highlights: Taylor Barnard climbed from sixth on the grid to take victory for DS Penske.
Nyck De Vries finished second from pole, taking 21 points for Mahindra Racing.
Edoardo Mortara completed a Mahindra one-two by finishing third from second on the grid.
Pascal Wehrlein fell away from third on the grid to finish fourteenth without scoring.
